title.narrative: East Africa Drought Appeal-Emergency Recovery Food Aid Response

description.narrative: The emergency and recovery response project intends to address the food shortage problem that has been caused rainfall failure in both farming seasons .i.e October 2008 to December 2008, short rains locally known as “Vuli” and March to July 2009 rains.This problem is not confide to Tanzania but the rest of Horn and East Africa. In Tanzania the project shall target 9,350 people out of 235,989 people affected by drought. Communities will participate in community projects that will benefit the community and receive food in return. However the disabled, elderly and infirm will receive free food handouts. Maize grain will be distributed. It costs £4 to provide one month’s supply of maize grain to an individual in Tanzania. There are 30 households (with about 200 people) whose homes were destroyed by landslides following some flash floods in November in the Diocese of same area. About 21 people died from the landslides. The project will supply maize grain, pulses and blankets to the 30 affected households. Since its inception Caritas Tanzania has been involved in dealing with relief food distribution among the population in the country. These include free food distribution and food for work programmes. Having its structures rooted to the grass root level CT has been implementing different relief programmes during calamities such as drought, earthquakes, fire, floods and refugees.
